content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Please create a u-shaped profile. The cross section should be 70mm wide and 40mm high. The web thickness needs to be 5mm. The profile should be 450mm long. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Below is the exact sequence, in plain words, that will turn the specification into geometry exclusively by means of the available function calls.  
(No function calls are executed yet.)

1. Establish a reference point  
   • Place the front-left-bottom corner of the profile at the global origin (0 , 0 , 0).  
   • Let the 450 mm length run in the positive Z-direction; the 70 mm width lies along +X; the 40 mm overall height lies along +Y.

2. Create the solid outer shell (one block, additive)  
   • x_size = 70 (mm) – full outside width  
   • y_size = 40 (mm) – full outside height  
   • z_size = 450 (mm) – full length  
   • basepoint (x,y,z) = (0, 0, 0)  
   • subtraction = False (this is the initial, positive volume)

3. Hollow the section to form the “U” (one block, subtractive)  
   • Wall / web thickness t = 5 mm.  
   • Inner cavity width = 70 − 2·t = 60 mm.  
   • Inner cavity height = 40 − t = 35 mm (the bottom flange stays 5 mm thick).  
   • x_size = 60 (mm)  
   • y_size = 35 (mm)  
   • z_size = 450 (mm) – same length, so the hollow runs the full profile  
   • basepoint (x,y,z) = (5, 5, 0)  
     – 5 mm inset from both side walls (X-direction) and from the bottom flange (Y-direction).  
   • subtraction = True (this removes the inner material, leaving the open-top U-shape).

4. Result  
   • A single continuous U-profile: outer 70 × 40 mm, wall thickness 5 mm, length 450 mm, open on top, fully connected and spatially accurate.

When you are ready, ask me to prepare the corresponding block-function payload exactly as outlined above; I will then supply the function-call JSON but will not execute it until explicitly instructed.
